note:
flashing the pinned reference image target/emu-ref/c976f17a9-esp32+test_shader_compile_incremental/fw-esp32v3 rather than building one: this payload's claim is a comparison against an emulated run of the SAME bytes (DD30), and the tree this runner stands in is not that commit. `scripts/emu/build-reference-image.sh esp32,test_shader_compile_incremental <commit> none` builds it in a detached worktree; the directory name is the provenance, and the runner checks its feature half.

THE FOUR SENTENCES ABOVE AND THE `source`/`capture` lines ARE THE RUNNER'S OWN; everything from here down was ADDED BY HAND at the desk (M5 P4, 2026-09-11), because the runner has no input for a desk's identity and none for the classic's standing rules. Nothing was changed, only added.

DESK. Board `domraem/dom-z-102`, chip revision v3.1 (espflash's own `Chip type: esp32 (revision v3.1)` line is in the transcript), MAC 30:76:f5:ec:f6:34, over the CH340K 1a86:7522 at locationID 0x1133000, port 3 of hub 0x1130000. The C6 A0:F2:62:87:B4:8C on port 2 of that hub was not touched. espflash 3.3.0. `--timeout-secs 420` rather than the default 120: the sentinel clock covers the flash, and on this cable a 4 MB write takes 2 min 27 s — at 120 s the runner SIGINTs espflash mid-write, which is what it did to this sitting's `boot-idle` step.

SECOND BOOT. espflash hard-resets after writing, so this capture is the boot AFTER the write, as every silicon capture of this board is. It is not the `boot-idle` second-boot rule, though: a harness image never mounts `lpfs`, so nothing formats an arena and there is no first/second-boot difference to have — which is why this payload's classic arm sets `second_boot: false`. An emulated twin of THIS transcript needs one run, not two.

THE WHOLE READ IS HERE. The `.txt` is the pty log `target/validate/shader-compile-stress.cap` byte for byte, 68,783 B, espflash's own output included; no range was trimmed and there is no separate `raw/` copy to make, unlike this sitting's hand-captured `boot-idle` pair where the reader's port was open at one baud while the other end spoke the other. Line 19 is not corrupt: it is the ROM and the second-stage bootloader printing at 115200 into a monitor opened at 921600, and the harness's in-band header sits at the end of it — `[fw-checks-header] {"schema":1,"payload":"shader-compile-stress","chip":"esp32v3","firmware_commit":"c976f17a9a1e","firmware_features":"default,esp32,float-f32,server,test_shader_compile_incremental","firmware_dirty":false}`. Read that line with `grep -a`; the file is binary to a text tool.

WHAT IT MEASURED, for the reader who wants the figures without the file: one case, `examples-basic`, `build=272.8ms ticks=92 max_slice=20.6ms max_slice_stage=Backend`, `peak_used 49016 / resident_used 14588 / after_drop_used 7848`, total `worst_peak_used 49016`. One sample: a harness figure is not a heartbeat figure, and nothing here drifted across the run's own 92 ticks in a way a second flash would resolve.

NO INSTRUMENT WAS ON A PAD, so the `pin` class is `modeled` for this capture as for every other in the sitting; the runner's trust table does not carry a `pin` row for this configuration and this note is where a reader is told.
